To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the teacher's role in organizing and facilitating collaborative inquiry practices is complex and multifaceted, and that the class's capacity for collaboration develops over time through a series of stages that can be described in terms of the community's capacity for collaborative inquiry.

the teacher's role in a collaborative classroom is to orchestrate the learning of the whole class and the development of the class's collective capacity for collaborative learning, and the class's collective ability to engage in collaborative learning develops over time.

the teacher in this case study used the following instructional strategies to organize and participate in the collaborative practices of his classroom: (a) he established and maintained an environment where students felt safe to express their ideas and where they were able to take risks, (b) he provided a balance of support and challenge to the students, and (c) he used the students' ideas to guide the mathematical content of the class.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the teacher in the instantiation of collaborative classroom practices, and how the community's capacity for collaborative inquiry develops over time.
how teachers can organize and participate in classroom practices that are consistent with the goals of recent mathematics education reform efforts.
the development of a teacher's capacity to enact a role that supports collaborative learning practices in a secondary mathematics classroom.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrates how a collaborative learning community can emerge and develop in a high school mathematics classroom.
collaborative practices are possible in secondary mathematics classrooms and can be organized and enacted in a variety of ways.
collaborative inquiry is a complex and challenging process for all members of a community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the teacher's role in supporting the development of collaborative practices is to provide the structure for the class to develop the capacity to participate in these practices over time.
the teacher's instructional practices and the class's evolving capacity to engage in collaboration are mutually constitutive, and that this process is mediated by the teacher's role in the classroom.

the teacher's role was one of a facilitator of learning, who was responsible for creating a learning environment where students were able to participate in collaborative mathematical inquiry practices, and that the development of this capacity occurred in a cyclical process of building a shared understanding of mathematical concepts, developing a shared understanding of collaborative practices, and engaging in collaborative inquiry activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

collaborative classroom practices are not only possible in secondary mathematics classrooms, but also that teachers can play a central role in supporting the development of a community's capacity to participate.

collaborative practices are not a panacea for the ills of mathematics education; however, they can provide students with opportunities to engage in meaningful mathematical practices and develop a deep understanding of mathematical concepts and procedures.
collaborative practices require the teacher to enact a new role that is distinct from traditional roles.
